{"task":{"request":"Write one read-only SQLite query. Include every customer ordered by id. Return columns customer_id, paid_order_count, net_cents. Count orders with status='paid' only. Net is paid order amounts minus all refunds attached to those paid orders; refunds on non-paid orders do not count. Include zero customers. Return {sql:string}.","schema":"CREATE TABLE customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, status TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER); CREATE TABLE refunds(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER, amount_cents INTEGER);"},"skill_catalog":{"ledger":"Deduplicate event ledgers and aggregate exact integer amounts.","schedule":"Find a common calendar interval across fixed UTC offsets.","dependencies":"Compute earliest starts and a critical path in an acyclic dependency graph.","selection":"Choose a finite bundle under budget, coverage and compatibility constraints.","memory":"Reduce scoped preference events into an auditable current snapshot.","sql":"Write read-only SQLite aggregates without multiplying joined rows.","file_edits":"Plan precise edits to local text files.","reminders":"Represent a reminder with an explicit time and delivery state.","conversation":"Produce a concise, sourced recap of a conversation.","incident_triage":"Record an operational incident and bounded diagnostic next steps."},"loaded_skills":{"sql":"Use only a SELECT statement or WITH followed by SELECT. Honor the requested output column order and deterministic row order. Pre-aggregate one-to-many child tables before joining them to another one-to-many relation, otherwise amounts and counts can multiply. Keep requested entities with zero qualifying rows using LEFT JOIN and COALESCE; filters on the optional side usually belong inside a subquery or ON condition. COUNT(*) after a left join can count a synthetic row; count a non-null child id instead. Choose latest attempts using the specified timestamp and tie-breaker before aggregating statuses. Preserve integer cents and do not assume hidden uniqueness constraints."},"handoff":{"candidate":{"answer":"WITH paid_order_totals AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.amount_cents - COALESCE(r.refund_cents, 0) AS net_cents
  FROM orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS refund_cents
    FROM refunds
    GROUP BY order_id
  ) AS r ON r.order_id = o.id
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
), customer_totals AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    COUNT(order_id) AS paid_order_count,
    SUM(net_cents) AS net_cents
  FROM paid_order_totals
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  c.id AS customer_id,
  COALESCE(ct.paid_order_count, 0) AS paid_order_count,
  COALESCE(ct.net_cents, 0) AS net_cents
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN customer_totals AS ct ON ct.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY c.id;"}}}
